cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a set of carved sago-palm-pith "belum" spirit figures on a stand, a documented traditional Melanau ritual object type from Sarawak used in healing ceremonies against malevolent spirits (tew). This is a well-attested Melanau craft, so it fits the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: belum; stand
physical.summary: Belum (image of a tew, i.e., malevolent spirit) (set of four with stand); carved of sago palm pith; a) crouching human figure, round hat with chevrons, left hand on heart, right arm along waist, four bands of triangles at waist, knees drawn up; square knob carved at bottom to fit into hole in stand; b) crouching human figure, round hat top folded over slightly, right hand on right shoulder, left arm along waist, three bands of triangles at waist, knees drawn up; square knob carved at bottom to fit into hole in stand; c) crouching human figure, hat with split down middle, right hand on right shoulder, left arm along waist, three bands of triangles at waist, knees drawn up; square knob carved at bottom to fit into hole in stand; d) crouching human figure, round hat, left hand on heart, right arm along waist, three bands of triangles at waist, knees drawn up; square knob carved at bottom to fit into hole in stand; e) stand: ovoid piece of wood with sides slightly bevelled, rectangular hole carved at north, south, east and west of ovoid to mount figures; together represents the air spirit Bilum Rabong Tebungan.
